# Engine

51 tools for Niagara systems and emitters with their modules, renderers, data interfaces, simulation stages and event handlers, and the engine's status.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_niagara_data_interface`

*Additive.*

Add a new UNiagaraDataInterface user-parameter binding to a Niagara system, inside an undo transaction, request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. A user parameter that already has this name and class is left as is (added false, already_exists true, nothing saved); one with this name and any other type is an error. The inverse is remove_niagara_data_interface.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the new user-parameter (no "User." prefix) |
| `data_interface_class` | string | yes | Data interface class name (e.g. "StaticMesh", "Texture"): a loaded data interface class with that name, else /Script/Niagara.NiagaraDataInterface&lt;Name> |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, data_interface_class: string, data_interface_class_path?: string, offset?: int, added?: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_niagara_emitter_from_template`

*Additive.*

Add a copy of a template emitter to a Niagara system (canonical path).  Loads the template/parent UNiagaraEmitter asset and adds a standalone copy of it to the system via FNiagaraEditorUtilities::AddEmitterToSystem — the same operation the Niagara editor's "Add Emitter" performs. This rebuilds the emitter's nodes and syncs the system overview graph, optionally names the new handle, then requests a compile and saves the system.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example") |
| `emitter_asset_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the source UNiagaraEmitter template (e.g. "/Niagara/DefaultAssets/Templates/Emitters/Fountain.Fountain") |
| `emitter_name` | string | no | Optional name for the new emitter handle; absent or empty keeps the name the engine generates from the source emitter. The engine sanitizes it and makes it unique among the system's emitters, so read emitter_handle_name for the stored name. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, source_emitter_asset: string, emitter_handle_id: string, emitter_handle_name: string, is_valid: bool, is_enabled: bool, emitters_before: int, total_emitters: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_niagara_event_handler`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add an event handler to a Niagara emitter (the writer for event_handler_count).  Constructs an FNiagaraEventScriptProperties (allocating its UNiagaraScript with usage ParticleEventScript, mirroring add_niagara_simulation_stage) and adds it via UNiagaraEmitter::AddEventHandler. Idempotent by source_event_name: if a handler for that event already exists it is returned (already_exists=true) without adding a duplicate. A spawn_number, max_events_per_frame or min_spawn_number that is not a JSON number is an error and nothing changes. The system is saved after modification. The handler's event-script graph is created in a default state -- full event wiring must be completed in the Niagara editor (reported honestly via note); the handler properties are persisted and re-readable.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example"). |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle within the system. |
| `source_event_name` | string | yes | Name of the source event this handler consumes (its identity key for idempotency). |
| `execution_mode` | string | no | Optional EveryParticle \| SpawnedParticles \| SingleParticle (default EveryParticle). |
| `spawn_number` | number | no | Optional int particles to spawn per event (SpawnedParticles mode). |
| `max_events_per_frame` | number | no | Optional int cap on events consumed per frame. |
| `min_spawn_number` | number | no | Optional int minimum spawn when random_spawn_number is set. |
| `random_spawn_number` | boolean | no | Optional bool: spawn a random count in [min_spawn_number, spawn_number]. |
| `source_emitter_id` | string | no | Optional GUID of the emitter handle that generates the event (default: this emitter). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, usage_id: string, source_event_name: string, execution_mode: string, spawn_number: int, max_events_per_frame: int, already_exists: bool, event_handler_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note: string }`

## `add_niagara_module_to_stack`

*Additive.*

Insert an engine module script into a Niagara emitter's particle stack.  Loads the module UNiagaraScript and inserts it into the emitter's ParticleSpawn or ParticleUpdate stack via FNiagaraStackGraphUtilities::AddScriptModuleToStack, at the end or at a chosen target_index, then recompiles and saves. Not idempotent: every call adds another module node.  NOTE: only the module's script-default inputs are applied — per-instance input overrides are out of scope (the response reports added_with_defaults=true). Stateless emitters (no editable graph) return a clean error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle to modify. |
| `module_script_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the module UNiagaraScript (e.g. "/Niagara/Modules/Update/Forces/GravityForce.GravityForce") |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn" (ParticleSpawnScript) or "update" (ParticleUpdateScript); defaults to "update" |
| `target_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based position in the stack; -1 (INDEX_NONE, the default) and any index past the end append. A value that is not a JSON number is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, module_script_path: string, script_group: string, target_index: int, module_node_name: string, added_with_defaults: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_niagara_renderer`

*Additive.*

Add a new renderer (Sprite / Ribbon / Mesh / Light / Decal) to a Niagara emitter, optionally with its properties seeded in the same call.  Creates a UNiagaraRendererProperties instance of the requested concrete class inside the emitter, as the Niagara editor does, optionally sets the Material UPROPERTY and the supplied properties (the keys set_niagara_renderer_properties takes, converted and clamped by reflection; enum keys fire PostEditChangeProperty), and appends it to the emitter's RendererProperties array, in one undo step. A Light is seeded with affects_translucency and alpha_scales_brightness true (the engine defaults are false), as the dedicated light-renderer tool seeded it; properties overrides either. Then requests a system compile and saves the asset. verified is true when the renderer is in the emitter's list and resolves that emitter; properties reads the stored values back. Each call adds one more renderer. An unknown renderer_type, a material_path that does not load as a material, an unknown key in properties, a numeric property given something other than a JSON number, or a value that does not convert is an error and nothing is created. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the renderer kept in memory.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example"). |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle (the human-readable name in the system's emitter list). |
| `renderer_type` | string | yes | One of "Sprite" / "Ribbon" / "Mesh" / "Light" / "Decal" (case-insensitive). |
| `material_path` | string | no | Optional asset path; sets the renderer's Material property (a class without one, such as Light, ignores it). If omitted, the renderer is added with a null material (still a valid empty renderer). |
| `properties` | object | no | Optional object of renderer properties to seed, with the keys and value forms of set_niagara_renderer_properties, e.g. {"radius_scale": 2, "use_inverse_squared_falloff": false, "color_add": {"X": 1, "Y": 0, "Z": 0}} for a Light (scales clamped at 0; affects_translucency and alpha_scales_brightness default to true) or {"decal_source_mode": "Emitter", "renderer_visibility": 1, "decal_screen_size_fade": 0.1} for a Decal. Keys the renderer class lacks are listed in not_applicable. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, renderer_type: string, renderer_class: string, renderer_index: int, material_path: string, applied: [string], not_applicable: [string], post_edit_fired: bool, properties: object, renderer_count: int, verified: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_niagara_simulation_stage`

*Additive.*

Add a generic simulation stage (UNiagaraSimulationStageGeneric) to one emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one undo step, then save the system. The stage gets stage_name as its SimulationStageName, iterates over Particles with execute behavior Always and dispatch type OneD, and runs iteration_count times in a row (default 1), read back in iteration_count; its graph starts in a default state, to be wired in the Niagara editor. An iteration_count that is not a JSON number from 0 to 65535 (the range the runtime honors; 0 skips the stage; a fraction is rounded), or an unknown system or emitter, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the stage kept in memory. Change its other settings with set_niagara_simulation_stage_properties; list stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle. |
| `stage_name` | string | yes | Name for the new simulation stage. |
| `iteration_count` | number | no | Optional number of times the stage runs in a row, from 0 to 65535 (rounded to a whole number); defaults to 1 |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, stage_name: string, requested_iteration_count: int, iteration_count: int, total_simulation_stages: int, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_niagara_system`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create an empty UNiagaraSystem asset at package_path/name and save it: its system spawn and update scripts are set up, but it has no emitters. Idempotent: a Niagara System already at that path is returned unchanged with created=false and already_exists=true, and nothing is saved; an asset of another class at that path is an error and nothing is written. Not an undo step. Next, add emitters with add_niagara_emitter_from_template, check the result with get_niagara_system_info or get_niagara_emitter_handles, and place it in a level with spawn_actor (type NiagaraActor). A failed save is an error, the new asset left in memory unsaved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | Asset name, e.g. 'NS_Sparks'; package_path/name must form a valid long package name. |
| `package_path` | string | no | Content folder as a long package path, e.g. '/Game/FX' (default /Game/Niagara); a trailing slash is ignored. |

**Returns:** `{ system_name: string, asset_path: string, created: bool, already_exists?: bool, saved?: bool, save_error?: string, emitter_count: int }`

## `duplicate_niagara_emitter_handle`

*Additive.*

Duplicate an emitter handle of a Niagara System asset under a new name, keeping its enabled state, in one undo step, then save the system. The source is found by display name (case-insensitive); an unknown system or source is an error and nothing changes. The stored name can differ from the one asked for, so read new_emitter_name. Returns the actual name and id of the copy plus total_emitters; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the copy kept in memory. Find handle names with get_niagara_emitter_handles; add an emitter asset instead with add_niagara_emitter_from_template; rename the copy with rename_niagara_emitter_handle.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it. |
| `source_emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle to copy (case-insensitive), as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it. |
| `new_emitter_name` | string | no | Name for the copy (default "&lt;source_emitter_name>_Copy"). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, source_emitter_name: string, new_emitter_name: string, new_emitter_id: string, is_valid: bool, total_emitters: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `duplicate_niagara_module_in_stack`

*Additive.*

Add another instance of a module to one emitter of a Niagara System asset: the module node named module_name (its function name, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives it) is found anywhere in the emitter graph and its script is added again to the script_group stack (spawn or update, default update; any other value reads as update) through FNiagaraStackGraphUtilities::AddScriptModuleToStack, in one undo step, then a system compile is requested and the system saved. The new module starts with the default inputs of the script; the input overrides of the source are not copied. target_index_override, a JSON number, sets its position; without it the position is the source index plus one among the module nodes of the emitter graph. An unknown system, emitter or module is an error; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Inputs: set_niagara_module_input; move: reorder_niagara_modules.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `module_name` | string | yes | Function name of the module node to duplicate, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn" or "update"; defaults to "update" |
| `target_index_override` | number | no | Optional position for the new module, a JSON number; defaults to the source index plus one among the module nodes of the emitter graph |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, source_module_name: string, new_module_name: string, inserted_index: int, duplicated: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `get_editor_status`

*Read-only.*

Prove the Unreal editor is alive and TICKING: a no-argument game-thread liveness/health probe, and the first call to make when the MCP bridge goes quiet. It runs on the GAME THREAD via the bridge's command drain, so a reply proves the game thread is pumping -- unlike a transport-only ping, which a wedged editor still answers. After a "Connection reset" use it to tell an editor CRASH (this errors, the reconnect refuses) from a mere tool TIMEOUT (this returns alive=true); call it twice and diff frame_counter to rule out a deadlock, since a frozen game thread replies once but never advances the frame (frame_count_render_thread is the render thread's own counter). Also reports whether PIE is running (pie_active / is_simulating) and the open editor world, without starting or stopping anything. Read-only and cheap; safe to call any time.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ alive: bool, gis_running: bool, exit_requested: bool, is_editor: bool, frame_counter: number, frame_count_render_thread: number, pie_active: bool, is_simulating: bool, editor_world: string, world_context_count: int }`

## `get_engine_info`

*Read-only.*

Read the GEngine object (engine_name, engine_class), the live UGameInstance (name, class, object path) and every world context with its world_name, world_type (Editor/PIE/Game/...) and has_game_instance flag. Use it to see how many worlds exist at once -- in co-op PIE the host and each client are SEPARATE world contexts, so this is how you confirm two PIE worlds are up before reading state that must be checked on both sides -- and which GameInstance class a running session picked. A UGameInstance only exists while PIE or a game world runs, so at rest game_instance_exists=false with empty strings is the normal answer, not an error. get_editor_status is the cheaper "is the editor alive" probe. Read-only.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ engine_name: string, engine_class: string, game_instance_exists: bool, game_instance_name: string, game_instance_class: string, game_instance_path: string, world_context_count: int, worlds: [{ world_name, world_type, has_game_instance }] }`

## `get_niagara_component_matrix`

*Read-only.*

Reads a Matrix (FMatrix4f) override parameter back off a spawned Niagara component — the round-trip reader for set_niagara_component_variable. UNiagaraComponent exposes no GetNiagaraVariableMatrix, so this reads the value straight out of the component's OverrideParameters store (FNiagaraParameterStore) by looking up the Matrix4 FNiagaraVariable; the override is stored as FMatrix44f. Returns found:false with an empty matrix (never a faked identity) when the variable has no local override on the component.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Owner actor identifier (internal name or editor label). |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | Niagara variable name to read. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, variable_name: string, variable_type: string, found: bool, matrix: [number x 16] }`

## `get_niagara_data_interfaces`

*Read-only.*

List all UNiagaraDataInterface user-parameter bindings on a Niagara system, or just the one named parameter_name, each with the name and property class of its UPROPERTYs (Transient and DuplicateTransient ones skipped). parameter_name is the user parameter's short name (no "User." prefix), the name the other data interface tools take; object_name and path_name name the data interface object itself; index is its slot in the system's data interface store. Read-only; a parameter_name that is not a data interface user parameter of the system is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional short name (no "User." prefix, case-insensitive) of one data interface user parameter to return. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, count: int, data_interfaces: [{ index, parameter_name, object_name, data_interface_class, data_interface_class_path, path_name, properties: [{ name, type }], property_count: int }] }`

## `get_niagara_effect_type`

*Read-only.*

Read which Niagara Effect Type asset a Niagara System asset uses, plus that effect type's settings: update_frequency and cull_reaction (as enum value names), allows_culling (bAllowCullingForLocalPlayers), and the scalability limits of its first system and emitter scalability entries: max_distance and max_instances (system), cull_by_distance (max_distance above 0) and scale_spawn_count (emitter SpawnCountScale). A system with no effect type, or an effect type without those entries, is a success with the defaults: an empty effect_type_path, None for both enums, allows_culling false, max_distance 0, max_instances 0, cull_by_distance false and scale_spawn_count 1. Read-only; an unknown system path is an error. Assign one with set_properties; the system's own flags and fixed bounds: get_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire" (the object path form also works). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, effect_type_path: string, update_frequency: string, cull_reaction: string, allows_culling: bool, max_distance: number, max_instances: int, cull_by_distance: bool, scale_spawn_count: number }`

## `get_niagara_emitter_data_interfaces`

*Read-only.*

List the Emitter Dependencies setting of one emitter of a Niagara System asset: the emitter bindings (FNiagaraDataInterfaceEmitterBinding) that order its particle scripts after other emitters when data interfaces read or write across emitters, each with the bound emitter_name and binding_mode (Self or Other); data_interface_count is the number of entries. It does not list the data interfaces themselves: get_niagara_data_interfaces lists the system's user-parameter data interfaces, and add_niagara_data_interface adds one. Read-only: it changes nothing. An emitter with no dependencies gives an empty list; a missing system or emitter handle is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, package or object form, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it, e.g. 'Fountain'. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, data_interface_count: int, data_interfaces: [{ emitter_name, binding_mode }] }`

## `get_niagara_emitter_handles`

*Read-only.*

List every emitter handle of a Niagara System asset, or just one chosen by display name or 0-based index, with its display name, id GUID, id name, enabled and valid flags, version GUID and, when it has emitter data, its local-space and deprecated flags, plus emitter_count (all handles of the system). Read-only; the names feed the other emitter tools. A name or index that matches no handle, or an emitter_index that is not a JSON number, is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it. |
| `emitter_name` | string | no | Optional display name of one handle to return (case-insensitive); when non-empty it wins over emitter_index. |
| `emitter_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based position in the emitter list of the system of one handle to return, used only when emitter_name is absent or empty. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_count: int, emitter_handles: [{ index: int, name: string, id: string, id_name: string, is_enabled: bool, is_valid: bool, emitter_version: string, is_local_space?: bool, is_deprecated?: bool }] }`

## `get_niagara_emitter_renderers`

*Read-only.*

List all renderers on a Niagara emitter (read-only).  Each entry also dumps the authored renderer UPROPERTYs (base bIsEnabled/SortOrderHint/MotionVectorSetting/bAllowInCullProxies plus the Sprite/Mesh-specific fields present on the concrete class) and, for Mesh renderers, the assigned static-mesh slots — so set_niagara_renderer_properties / set_niagara_mesh_renderer_mesh round-trip.

|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |

## `get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary`

*Read-only.*

Read one emitter of a Niagara System asset in a single flat reply: simulation target (CPUSim or GPUComputeSim), bounds mode (Dynamic, Fixed or Programmable) and its fixed box as 'X=.. Y=.. Z=..' strings, particle allocation mode and pre-allocation count, GPU spawn cap per frame (max_gpu_particles), local-space, determinism and persistent-ID flags, and how many renderers, event handlers and simulation stages it has. Read-only: it changes nothing and compiles nothing. The four *_module_count fields all count the function-call nodes (modules and dynamic inputs) of the emitter's one shared script graph, so they are always equal; list_niagara_modules lists a stack's modules. A missing system or emitter handle is an error. Change these settings with set_niagara_emitter_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Content path of the UNiagaraSystem asset, package or object form, e.g. '/Game/FX/NS_Sparks'. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle, as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it, e.g. 'Fountain'. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, sim_target: string, bounds_mode: string, bounds_min: string, bounds_max: string, allocation_mode: string, pre_allocation_count: int, max_gpu_particles: int, local_space: bool, deterministic: bool, requires_persistent_ids: bool, update_module_count: int, spawn_module_count: int, emitter_spawn_module_count: int, emitter_update_module_count: int, renderer_count: int, event_handler_count: int, simulation_stage_count: int }`

| `handle_index` | number | no | Optional fallback when multiple emitters share a name (0-based). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, simulation_stage_count: int, total_simulation_stages: int, simulation_stages: [{ index, stage_name, class, enabled, iteration_source? }] }`

## `get_niagara_system_info`

*Read-only.*

Reads metadata for a UNiagaraSystem: emitter count, exposed user parameters, and its warmup and determinism settings (warmup_time in seconds, warmup_tick_count, warmup_tick_delta, needs_warmup, deterministic). Read-only; change the warmup with set_properties, determinism with set_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. /Game/Niagara/NS_Example or /Game/Niagara/NS_Example.NS_Example) |

**Returns:** `{ system_name: string, system_path: string, emitter_count: int, num_user_parameters: int, warmup_time: number, warmup_tick_count: int, warmup_tick_delta: number, needs_warmup: bool, deterministic: bool, user_parameters: [{ name, type }] }`

## `get_niagara_user_parameter`

*Read-only.*

Read a user-exposed parameter's current value from a Niagara System's exposed store.  Resolves the parameter by short name (no "User." prefix) and the supplied ``type`` token, reads the POD value back. Round-trip companion to set_niagara_user_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | User parameter name (without the "User." prefix). |
| `type` | string | no | Type token: Float\|Vector\|Vec2\|Vec4\|Color\|Bool\|Int (case-insensitive); defaults to Float |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, parameter_type: string, found: bool, value_read_back?: number|bool|[number...] }`

## `list_niagara_data_interface_classes`

*Read-only.*

Enumerate every concrete UNiagaraDataInterface subclass registered in this process via TObjectIterator. Skips Abstract (those are base classes only). Used to discover what data-interface class strings are valid for add_niagara_data_interface.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ count: int, classes: [{class_name, class_path, display_name, abstract, class_flags}] }`

## `list_niagara_modules`

*Read-only.*

List the module function-call nodes on one stack, or both stacks, of a Niagara emitter (read-only), optionally just the module with a given name. Resolves the emitter's spawn or update group graph (script_group, default "update"; "all" reads both and also groups them as spawn[] and update[]) via the export-safe ResolveEmitterOutputNode + UNiagaraGraph::GetNodesOfClass path, then reports each UNiagaraNodeFunctionCall: index (its position in its stack), module_name (GetFunctionName), node_guid, function_script(+class), is_enabled (IsNodeEnabled), is_deprecated, input/output pin counts. Honest-empty modules:[] when the stack has no modules or the graph is not resolvable (a note is returned); a module_name that matches no module is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn", "update" or "all" (both stacks); defaults to "update". |
| `module_name` | string | no | Optional module name (GetFunctionName, case-sensitive): return only that module; an error when no module of the stack(s) has it. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_count: int, total_modules_in_stack: int, modules: [{ index, script_group, module_name, node_guid, function_script?, function_script_class?, is_enabled, is_deprecated, input_pin_count, output_pin_count, total_modules_in_stack }], note?: string, spawn?: [{...}], update?: [{...}], spawn_module_count?: int, update_module_count?: int, spawn_note?: string, update_note?: string }`

## `list_niagara_renderer_classes`

*Read-only.*

Enumerate every concrete UNiagaraRendererProperties subclass registered in this process via TObjectIterator. Skips Abstract (those are base classes only). Used to discover what renderer_class strings are valid for add_niagara_renderer.

No parameters.

**Returns:** `{ count: int, classes: [{class_name, class_path, display_name, abstract, class_flags}] }`

## `move_niagara_simulation_stage`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move one simulation stage of an emitter of a Niagara System asset to target_index, its 0-based place in the stage list, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. The stage is found by stage_index (preferred) or stage_name (its SimulationStageName, case-insensitive); one is required. A stage that is not found, a target_index missing or outside the current list, a stage_index or target_index that is not a JSON number, or an unknown system or emitter is an error and nothing changes. Idempotent: a stage already at target_index is a success with moved=false, already_at_target=true and saved=false, nothing written. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. List stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages; take one out with remove_niagara_simulation_stage.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle owning the stage. |
| `target_index` | number | yes | Required 0-based target index the stage should occupy after the move, a JSON number in [0, total_simulation_stages). |
| `stage_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based index into the emitter's simulation stages, a JSON number; takes precedence over stage_name when both are supplied. |
| `stage_name` | string | no | Optional SimulationStageName to match if stage_index is not supplied. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path, emitter_name, stage_index, stage_name, stage_class, target_index, moved, already_at_target, before_index, after_index, total_simulation_stages, saved, save_error? }`

## `remove_niagara_data_interface`

*Destructive.*

Remove a UNiagaraDataInterface user-parameter binding from a Niagara system by name, inside an undo transaction, request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. A name with no user parameter, or a user parameter that is not a data interface, is an error and nothing is changed.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the user-parameter to remove (no "User." prefix) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, data_interface_class: string, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_niagara_emitter_handle`

*Destructive.*

Remove one emitter handle from a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the system. The handle is chosen by display name (case-insensitive) or, when emitter_name is absent or empty, by 0-based emitter_index. An unknown system, name or index, or an emitter_index that is not a JSON number, is an error and nothing changes. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Returns the removed name and id and the emitter counts before and after. List handles with get_niagara_emitter_handles; to keep an emitter but stop it, use set_niagara_emitter_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | no | Optional display name of the emitter handle to remove |
| `emitter_index` | number | no | Optional zero-based index; used if emitter_name not provided |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, removed_emitter_name: string, removed_emitter_id: string, emitters_before: int, emitters_after: int, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_niagara_event_handler`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove an event handler from a Niagara emitter by its usage_id.  Calls UNiagaraEmitter::RemoveEventHandlerByUsageId. Idempotent: if no handler with that usage_id exists it reports already_removed without error. The system is saved after a removal.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle within the system. |
| `usage_id` | string | yes | The handler's usage_id (as returned by add_niagara_event_handler / get_niagara_event_handlers). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, usage_id: string, already_removed: bool, removed: bool, event_handler_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_niagara_module_from_stack`

*Destructive.*

Remove a UNiagaraNodeFunctionCall module from a Niagara emitter's spawn or update graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `module_name` | string | yes | Display name of the module function-call node to remove |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn" or "update"; defaults to "update" |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, removed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_niagara_renderer`

*Destructive.*

Take the renderer at renderer_index (0-based, in get_niagara_emitter_renderers order) out of one emitter of a Niagara System asset, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. renderer_index is required and must be a JSON number of 0 or more; an index out of range, an empty renderer slot, or an unknown system or emitter is an error and nothing changes. The renderers after it move down one index. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. Returns the class of the renderer taken out and the count left. Add one with add_niagara_renderer; change one with set_niagara_renderer_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `renderer_index` | number | yes | 0-based index into the emitter's renderers list, a JSON number (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers to find the index) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, removed_renderer_index: int, removed_renderer_class: string, renderer_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_niagara_simulation_stage`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Remove one simulation stage from an emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by stage_index (0-based, preferred) or stage_name (its SimulationStageName, case-insensitive), in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. One of the two is required, and a stage_index that is not a JSON number is an error. Idempotent: a stage that is not found (an index out of range falls back to stage_name) is a success with removed=false, already_removed=true and saved=false, nothing written. An unknown system or emitter is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error, the removal kept in memory. List stages with get_niagara_simulation_stages; reorder them with move_niagara_simulation_stage; add one with add_niagara_simulation_stage.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle owning the stage. |
| `stage_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based index into the emitter's simulation stages, a JSON number; takes precedence over stage_name when both are supplied. |
| `stage_name` | string | no | Optional SimulationStageName to match if stage_index is not supplied (matches add_niagara_simulation_stage's name). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path, emitter_name, stage_index, stage_name, stage_class, removed, already_removed, total_simulation_stages, saved, save_error? }`

## `remove_niagara_user_parameter`

*Destructive.*

Remove one plain user parameter (the User. namespace: a float, int, bool, vector, color...) from a Niagara System asset, in one undo step; the asset is marked dirty, not saved, as set_niagara_user_parameter leaves it (save_asset keeps it). Inverse of set_niagara_user_parameter, which adds the parameter when it is missing. A data interface user parameter is refused (remove_niagara_data_interface removes those), and so is a name the system has no user parameter for, with nothing changed. The reply re-reads the store (still_present). Read: get_niagara_user_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | User parameter name (without the "User." prefix). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, parameter_type: string, removed: bool, still_present: bool }`

## `rename_niagara_emitter_handle`

*Destructive.*

Rename an emitter handle of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, then save the system. The engine sanitizes the name and makes it unique among the emitters of the system, so read new_name and verified (false when the stored name differs from the request). A name the engine takes as the current one (the same after sanitizing, case-sensitive, ignoring a trailing number) is a success with renamed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. An unknown system or current_name is an error. A failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. List names with get_niagara_emitter_handles; copy a handle under a new name with duplicate_niagara_emitter_handle.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire"; the call fails without it. |
| `current_name` | string | yes | Current display name of the emitter handle (case-insensitive), as get_niagara_emitter_handles lists it. |
| `new_name` | string | yes | Requested display name; it may come back sanitized or with a numeric suffix. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, old_name: string, new_name: string, verified: bool, renamed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `reorder_niagara_modules`

*Destructive.*

Move a module node, found by function name (case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives it) anywhere in the graph of one emitter of a Niagara System asset, to target_index by reordering the graph node array in place (pins and inputs kept), in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. target_index, old_index and new_index count all module nodes of the emitter graph in node order, as list_niagara_modules reports index; target_index is required, a JSON number of 0 or more, and one past the last is clamped to it. A module already in place is still saved and reordered is always true, so compare old_index with new_index. An unknown system, emitter or module is an error; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. Insert at a position: add_niagara_module_to_stack with target_index.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `module_name` | string | yes | Function name of the module node to move, case-sensitive, as list_niagara_modules gives module_name |
| `target_index` | number | yes | Target position, a JSON number of 0 or more, counted over the module nodes of the emitter graph; clamped to the last; the call fails without it |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn" or "update"; defaults to "update" |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, old_index: int, new_index: int, target_index: int, reordered: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_component_fixed_bounds`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the fixed-bounds override of the Niagara component on a placed actor in the editor world (the first UNiagaraComponent of the actor found by internal name or label) to the local-space box min..max, then read it back. The override lives only in memory on that component: it is not a saved property, so it is lost when the level reloads and is not carried into PIE, and it makes no undo step and does not dirty the level. Repeating the call with the same box gives the same result. An actor that is missing or has no Niagara component is an error and nothing changes. For bounds that persist with the asset, set bounds_mode Fixed and the box on an emitter with set_niagara_emitter_properties; place a Niagara actor with spawn_actor (type NiagaraActor).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Internal name or editor label of an actor in the editor world that has a Niagara component, as get_actors_in_level lists it, e.g. 'NiagaraActor_0'. |
| `min` | array | no | Box minimum corner in the component's local space, [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [-500, -500, 0]; a missing or short array reads as [0, 0, 0], and it is not checked against max. |
| `max` | array | no | Box maximum corner in the component's local space, [x, y, z] in centimetres, e.g. [500, 500, 800]; a missing or short array reads as [0, 0, 0]. |

**Returns:** `{ actor_name: string, applied: bool, bounds_valid: bool, min_read_back: [number, number, number], max_read_back: [number, number, number] }`

## `set_niagara_component_variable`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set a user parameter (variable override) on the Niagara component of an editor-world actor, found by internal name or label, the first UNiagaraComponent on it used: type says what value holds -- float, int, bool, vec2, vector, vec4, position, color, quat, matrix or object -- and the component's own SetVariable&lt;Type> runs, then the value is read back. The override is added locally when the component has none for that name. One undo step; nothing is saved (save_level for a placed actor). The fixed bounds of the component are set_niagara_component_fixed_bounds; a parameter's default in the system asset is set_niagara_user_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `actor_name` | string | yes | The actor carrying the Niagara component (internal name or editor label) |
| `variable_name` | string | yes | The user parameter, e.g. "User.SpawnRate" or "SpawnRate" |
| `type` | string | yes | One of float, int, bool, vec2, vector, vec4, position, color, quat, matrix, object |
| `value` | any | no | The value: a number (float, int), a bool, an array of 2/3/4 numbers (vec2, vector and position, vec4, color as [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A]), [x, y, z, w] (quat), 16 numbers in row-major order (matrix), or an asset path (object) |

**Returns:** `{ the setter's reply: actor_name, variable_name, the value read back }`

## `set_niagara_data_interface_array`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replace the contents of a numeric array on an array user-parameter data interface of a Niagara System asset (FloatData by default, IntData on the int32 array DI) with values, in an undo transaction that records the DI, then request a recompile and save the system; success requires the save. Every value must be a finite JSON number; an int array stores it truncated toward zero. A value of another type, an unknown system or data interface, an array_property the DI lacks, or an array of structs (Vector, Color, Position) is an error and nothing changes. There is no no-op check: the same values are written and saved again. The reply reads the stored array back. The DI must exist (add_niagara_data_interface); curve DIs: set_niagara_data_interface_curve; inspect it with get_niagara_data_interfaces.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the user-parameter array DI (no "User." prefix) |
| `values` | array | yes | Array of finite JSON numbers to store (replaces all existing array contents); any other element is an error |
| `array_property` | string | no | Optional array UPROPERTY to set (default "FloatData"; e.g. "IntData" for the int32 array DI) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, array_property: string, element_type: string, count: int, values: [number], set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_data_interface_asset`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Points an object property of a user-parameter data interface on a Niagara system at an asset (e.g. the mesh of a StaticMesh DI, the texture of a Texture DI), inside an undo transaction, reads it back, requests a system recompile and saves the system; success requires the read-back and the save. The DI must already exist (add_niagara_data_interface); property_name picks the property, else the first hard object property in reflection order. The asset must load and be of the property's class, else it is an error and nothing is written. For non-asset fields use set_niagara_data_interface_default.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the user-parameter DI to mutate |
| `asset_path` | string | no | Asset path of the UObject to assign (must be the right subclass) |
| `property_name` | string | no | Optional FObjectProperty name on the DI; defaults to the first FObjectProperty |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, property_name: string, asset_path: string, set: bool (the property reads back the asset), saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_data_interface_curve`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Replaces all keys of one FRichCurve property on a curve user-parameter data interface of a Niagara system with the given time/value keys (an empty array clears it), rebuilds the DI's lookup table, requests a recompile and saves the system, inside an undo transaction that records the DI; success requires the save. The DI must already exist (add_niagara_data_interface) and curve_property must name an FRichCurve on it: Curve by default, XCurve/YCurve/ZCurve (WCurve too on Vector4) on vector curve DIs, RedCurve/GreenCurve/BlueCurve/AlphaCurve on color curve DIs. Every key must be an object whose time and value are finite JSON numbers, or it is an error and nothing changes. For array DIs use set_niagara_data_interface_array.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the user-parameter curve DI (no "User." prefix) |
| `keys` | array | yes | Array of { time: number, value: number } keys to set (replaces all existing keys on the channel) |
| `curve_property` | string | no | Optional FRichCurve UPROPERTY to author (default "Curve"; e.g. "RedCurve"/"XCurve" on Color/Vector curve DIs) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, curve_property: string, key_count: int, keys: [{time,value}], set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_data_interface_default`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Writes one property of a user-parameter data interface on a Niagara system from text parsed by the property's ImportText, so any type it accepts works ("1.5", "(X=1,Y=2,Z=3)", "(R=1,G=0,B=0,A=1)", an enum name), inside an undo transaction, then requests a system recompile and saves the system; success requires the save. A missing DI or property, or text that does not parse, is an error and the DI is left untouched. value echoes the request; value_read_back is the stored value exported as text. List the DI's properties with get_niagara_data_interfaces; for asset references use set_niagara_data_interface_asset.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | Short name of the user-parameter DI to mutate |
| `property_name` | string | yes | Name of the FProperty on the DI to set |
| `value` | string | yes | String representation of the value (parsed by FProperty::ImportText_Direct) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, property_name: string, value: string, value_read_back: string, set: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_emitter_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Change any settings of ONE emitter of a Niagara System asset, found by handle name, in one call: enabled, simulation target (CPU or GPU), local space, determinism, bounds mode and fixed box, particle allocation mode and pre-allocation count, GPU particle cap and persistent IDs. Pass only the settings to change; each is validated and applied by its own step, in the order listed here, the system recompiled where the setting needs it and saved, and the call stops at the first setting refused, with applied listing those already changed. System-level settings (warmup, effect type, determinism of the system) are properties of the system asset: set_properties with save=true. get_niagara_emitter_info reads an emitter back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Niagara System asset path, e.g. "/Game/FX/NS_Fire" |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Emitter handle name as shown in the system (case-insensitive) |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional: enable or disable the emitter handle |
| `sim_target` | string | no | Optional: "CPUSim" or "GPUComputeSim" |
| `local_space` | boolean | no | Optional: simulate particles in the emitter's local space (true) or world space (false) |
| `deterministic` | boolean | no | Optional: the emitter's determinism flag |
| `bounds_mode` | string | no | Optional: "Dynamic", "Fixed" or "Programmable" |
| `bounds_min` | string | no | Optional fixed-bounds minimum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=-50 Y=-50 Z=0" |
| `bounds_max` | string | no | Optional fixed-bounds maximum corner as an FVector string, e.g. "X=50 Y=50 Z=100" |
| `allocation_mode` | string | no | Optional: "AutomaticEstimate", "ManualEstimate" or "FixedCount" |
| `pre_allocation_count` | number | no | Optional particle count to allocate up front; needs allocation_mode |
| `max_gpu_particles` | number | no | Optional cap on GPU particles (0 = no cap) |
| `requires_persistent_ids` | boolean | no | Optional: whether particles carry persistent IDs |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, applied: { setting: that setting's reply }, failed?: { label, command, error } (when a setting is refused) }`

## `set_niagara_mesh_renderer_mesh`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Assign a static mesh into a Niagara Mesh renderer's Meshes[] slot.  Resolves (or grows the array to) the slot index, loads the UStaticMesh, and sets the slot's inner .Mesh via reflection on the FNiagaraMeshRendererMeshProperties element. Then requests a system compile and saves; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. add_niagara_renderer type=Mesh leaves Meshes empty (renders nothing); this is the command that makes a Mesh renderer actually draw. A renderer_index or slot that is not a JSON number is an error and nothing changes. Idempotent: re-assigning the same mesh to the same slot does not grow the array, writes nothing and saves nothing (already_assigned=true, saved=false).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `renderer_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the Mesh renderer (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers). |
| `mesh_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UStaticMesh to assign (e.g. "/Engine/BasicShapes/Cube"). |
| `slot` | number | no | Optional 0-based slot index into Meshes[] (default 0). The array is grown with default elements up to this index if needed. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path, emitter_name, renderer_index, renderer_class, slot, mesh_path, mesh_count, already_assigned: bool, saved: bool, save_error? }`

## `set_niagara_module_enabled`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Enable or disable a UNiagaraNodeFunctionCall module in a Niagara emitter's spawn or update graph.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `module_name` | string | yes | Display name of the module to toggle |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool; defaults to true |
| `script_group` | string | no | Optional "spawn" or "update"; defaults to "update" |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, script_group: string, module_name: string, previous_enabled?: bool, enabled: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_module_input`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Override a Niagara module input by writing the rapid-iteration store. Locates the module function-call node (by its module_node_name, as returned by add_niagara_module_to_stack) on the emitter's spawn or update stack, matches the input by its leaf name, and writes the value into the owning group script's RapidIterationParameters store. The system is recompiled and saved. value is required: a JSON number for a float or int input, [x, y, z] for a vector, [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] for a color; a missing or malformed one is an error and nothing changes. HONEST GATE: bool / enum / data-interface / object inputs are not rapid-iteration eligible and return a clean error. The packed value_type must also match the input's actual type or a clean error is returned. Read it back with get_niagara_module_input.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System (e.g. "/Game/Niagara/NS_Example"). |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Display name of the emitter handle. |
| `module_node_name` | string | yes | The module function-call node name (from add_niagara_module_to_stack's module_node_name). |
| `input_name` | string | yes | Leaf name of the module input (e.g. "Drag" for "Module.Drag"). |
| `value_type` | string | no | One of "float", "int", "vector", or "color"; defaults to "float" |
| `value` | any | no | Required. For float/int: a JSON number. For vector: [x, y, z], numbers within the float range. For color: [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], alpha 1 when omitted. A missing or malformed value is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, module_node_name: string, input_name: string, value_type: string, ri_param_name: string, verified: bool, success: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `set_niagara_renderer_material`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the Material UPROPERTY on a Niagara renderer (Sprite, Ribbon, Mesh or Decal: any renderer class with a Material property).  Loads the material, sets it on the renderer's public Material field, requests a system compile and saves; a failed save makes success false, with saved=false and save_error. A renderer that already uses that material is a success with changed=false and saved=false, and nothing is written. A renderer_index that is not a JSON number, or a renderer class without a Material property (Light), is an error. Reads back to verify the material path is now bound, and returns the material it replaced.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `renderer_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the renderer (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers to find the index) |
| `material_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the UMaterialInterface to assign. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, emitter_name: string, renderer_index: int, renderer_class: string, previous_material_path: string, material_path: string, verified: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `set_niagara_renderer_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set properties of one renderer (Sprite, Mesh, Ribbon, Light or Decal) of a Niagara emitter, found by emitter_name and renderer_index, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. Use it over set_properties, which neither finds the renderer nor applies ClampMin/ClampMax, compiles or saves. Only supplied fields are written; enum fields (alignment, facing_mode, sort_mode, motion_vector_setting, decal_source_mode) also fire PostEditChangeProperty. Every field is converted before the first write, so a value that does not convert (an unknown enum name, an array for a struct field) or a non-number renderer_index is an error and nothing changes. Values already held: changed=false, saved=false. Keys the renderer class lacks are listed in not_applicable. A failed save makes success false with save_error. Materials: set_niagara_renderer_material; mesh: set_niagara_mesh_renderer_mesh; read back: get_niagara_renderer_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle. |
| `renderer_index` | number | yes | 0-based index of the renderer (use get_niagara_emitter_renderers). |
| `enabled` | string | no | Optional bool: base bIsEnabled (also accepted as renderer_enabled). |
| `sort_order_hint` | string | no | Optional int: base SortOrderHint. |
| `motion_vector_setting` | string | no | Optional enum name: base MotionVectorSetting (e.g. "AutoDetect"/"Precise"/"Disable"). |
| `allow_in_cull_proxies` | string | no | Optional bool: base bAllowInCullProxies. |
| `alignment` | string | no | Optional enum name (Sprite): Alignment (e.g. "Unaligned"/"VelocityAligned"/"CustomAlignment"/"Automatic"). |
| `facing_mode` | string | no | Optional enum name (Sprite ENiagaraSpriteFacingMode or Mesh ENiagaraMeshFacingMode, resolved by class): FacingMode. |
| `sort_mode` | string | no | Optional enum name (Sprite/Mesh): SortMode (e.g. "None"/"ViewDepth"/"ViewDistance"/"CustomAscending"/"CustomDescending"). |
| `sub_image_size` | string | no | Optional {X,Y} object (Sprite/Mesh): SubImageSize; an [x,y] array is an error. |
| `macro_uv_radius` | string | no | Optional float (Sprite): MacroUVRadius. |
| `pivot_in_uv_space` | string | no | Optional {X,Y} object (Sprite): PivotInUVSpace; an [x,y] array is an error. |
| `cast_shadows` | string | no | Optional bool (Sprite): bCastShadows. |
| `renderer_visibility` | string | no | Optional int (Sprite): RendererVisibility tag value. |
| `override_materials` | string | no | Optional bool (Mesh): bOverrideMaterials. |
| `mesh_bounds_scale` | string | no | Optional {X,Y,Z} object (Mesh): MeshBoundsScale; an [x,y,z] array is an error. |
| `locked_axis` | string | no | Optional {X,Y,Z} object (Mesh): LockedAxis; an [x,y,z] array is an error. |
| `use_inverse_squared_falloff` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bUseInverseSquaredFalloff. |
| `affects_translucency` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bAffectsTranslucency. |
| `allow_mega_lights` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bAllowMegaLights. |
| `mega_lights_cast_shadows` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bMegaLightsCastShadows. |
| `alpha_scales_brightness` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bAlphaScalesBrightness. |
| `override_inverse_exposure_blend` | string | no | Optional bool (Light): bOverrideInverseExposureBlend. |
| `radius_scale` | string | no | Optional float (Light, ClampMin=0): RadiusScale. |
| `default_exponent` | string | no | Optional float (Light, ClampMin=0): DefaultExponent (used when use_inverse_squared_falloff=false). |
| `specular_scale` | string | no | Optional float (Light, ClampMin=0): SpecularScale. |
| `diffuse_scale` | string | no | Optional float (Light, ClampMin=0): DiffuseScale. |
| `color_add` | string | no | Optional {X,Y,Z} object (Light): ColorAdd (FVector3f RGB shift); an [x,y,z] array is an error. |
| `inverse_exposure_blend` | string | no | Optional float (Light): InverseExposureBlend. |
| `decal_screen_size_fade` | string | no | Optional float (Decal): DecalScreenSizeFade. |
| `decal_source_mode` | string | no | Optional enum name/int (Decal): SourceMode ("Particles"/"Emitter"); fires PostEditChangeProperty so UpdateSourceModeDerivates runs. |

**Returns:** `{ system_path, emitter_name, renderer_index, renderer_class, applied:[prop names written], not_applicable:[input keys], post_edit_fired: bool, properties:{round-trip dump}, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?, note? }`

## `set_niagara_simulation_stage_properties`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the enum, bool, name and FIntPoint properties of one generic simulation stage (UNiagaraSimulationStageGeneric) of a Niagara emitter, found by stage_index or stage_name, in one undo step, then request a system compile and save. Use it over set_properties, which neither finds the stage nor applies ClampMin/ClampMax, compiles or saves. Only supplied fields are written; enabled goes through SetEnabled and enum writes fire PostEditChangeProperty. Every field is converted before the first write, so a value that does not convert, a non-bool enabled or a non-number stage_index is an error and nothing changes. Values already held: changed=false, saved=false. Binding fields (num_iterations, iteration_count, element_count_x|y|z, data_interface) go to not_supported, never written; add_niagara_simulation_stage sets the iteration count. A failed save makes success false with save_error. List: get_niagara_simulation_stages.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `emitter_name` | string | yes | Name of the emitter handle owning the stage. |
| `stage_index` | number | no | Optional 0-based index into the emitter's simulation stages (use add_niagara_simulation_stage / get_niagara_emitter_runtime_summary); takes precedence over stage_name |
| `stage_name` | string | no | Optional SimulationStageName to match if stage_index is not supplied. |
| `name` | string | no | Optional FName: SimulationStageName (renames the stage; also accepted as simulation_stage_name). |
| `enabled` | boolean | no | Optional bool: base bEnabled (written via SetEnabled). |
| `iteration_source` | string | no | Optional enum name: IterationSource (Particles\|DataInterface\|DirectSet). |
| `execute_behavior` | string | no | Optional enum name: ExecuteBehavior (Always\|OnSimulationReset\|NotOnSimulationReset). |
| `disable_partial_particle_update` | string | no | Optional bool: bDisablePartialParticleUpdate. |
| `particle_iteration_state_enabled` | string | no | Optional bool: bParticleIterationStateEnabled. |
| `particle_iteration_state_range` | string | no | Optional {X,Y} object: ParticleIterationStateRange (FIntPoint; the generic struct path needs the object form, not a [x,y] array). |
| `gpu_dispatch_force_linear` | string | no | Optional bool: bGpuDispatchForceLinear. |
| `direct_dispatch_type` | string | no | Optional enum name: DirectDispatchType (OneD\|TwoD\|ThreeD). |
| `direct_dispatch_element_type` | string | no | Optional enum name: DirectDispatchElementType (NumThreads\|NumThreadsNoClipping\|NumGroups). |

**Returns:** `{ system_path, emitter_name, stage_index, stage_name, stage_class, applied:[prop names written], not_applicable:[keys], not_supported:[binding keys], enabled?: bool, post_edit_fired: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?, note? }`

## `set_niagara_user_parameter`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Set the default value of one user parameter (the User. namespace) of a Niagara System asset in one undo step, adding the parameter when the system has none of that name and type; the asset is marked dirty, not saved (save_asset keeps it). type picks Float, Vector, Vec2, Vec4, Color, Bool or Int; without it a vector, vec2, vec4 or color key picks that type, else Float. A missing value, or one not of the JSON type the parameter takes, is an error with nothing written. A parameter already holding the value is a success with changed=false and value_set=false, nothing written. verified means the value reads back as sent. Read it with get_niagara_user_parameter; inverse: remove_niagara_user_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system_path` | string | yes | Asset path of the Niagara System. |
| `parameter_name` | string | yes | User parameter name (without the "User." prefix). |
| `type` | string | no | Optional type token: Float\|Vector\|Vec2\|Vec4\|Color\|Bool\|Int (case-insensitive); when omitted a vector, vec2, vec4 or color key picks that type, else Float |
| `value` | any | no | The value of a Float (a number), Int (a whole number) or Bool (true or false) parameter; those types fail without it or with another JSON type |
| `vector` | array | no | [X, Y, Z], 3 numbers, the value of a Vector parameter (required for it; also picks type Vector when type is omitted) |
| `vec2` | array | no | [X, Y], 2 numbers, the value of a Vec2 parameter (required for it) |
| `vec4` | array | no | [X, Y, Z, W], 4 numbers, the value of a Vec4 parameter (required for it) |
| `color` | array | no | [R, G, B] or [R, G, B, A] linear color of a Color parameter, A 1 when omitted (required for it) |

**Returns:** `{ system_path: string, parameter_name: string, parameter_type: string, value_set: bool, changed: bool, value_read_back?: number|bool|[number...], verified: bool, note?: string }`
